### problem_chain

- **Root problem.** The customer asks for "the smallest payment Kestrel will take on it today under whatever payment plan you offer" on the turned-in Corvalis. That maps to balloon_ext_return_balance_plan (on_request, `returned` contract), whose target tool is `pay_return_balance_installment_2f123e0a` (owner=user).
- **The root rule's prerequisite sentences and the opening world:**

| edge | sentence | false at opening because | resolved by (found from the depended-on rule) | kind |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| plan←mileage | "…fixed only after the excess mileage charge for the return stands billed on the contract." | the seed has 47 `balloon_transactions` rows and none with event_type `balloon_return_charge`; fees_due_balance 25.00 is the 2025-12-06 late charge only | mileage rule "sets the excess mileage charge billed once…", via bill_excess_mileage_charge_7a491561 | value_input (`mileage_billed`) |
| plan←wear | "…not fixed until the excess wear charge for the return stands billed…" | same: no return_charge rows | wear rule, via bill_excess_wear_charge_ce1b5dd4 | value_input (`wear_billed`) |
| plan←fee | "Before … the return fee for the return must stand billed…" | same | fee rule, via bill_return_fee_2252d2f2 | value_input (`fee_billed`) |

- **Tree:** three prerequisite problems (mileage, wear, fee, all agent-owned, all `prerequisite: []`) under a user-owned root. There are 3 value_input edges, at least the required max(3−1, 1) = 2. The tree is acyclic. The customer's own write is the root, so at least one problem is a user write.
- **Topological order:** {mileage, wear, fee} in any order, then plan.
- **Parallel-edge terminal state.** Each charge tool adds its own amount to fees_due_balance, and no charge computation reads fees_due or another charge. So every order of the three yields the same rows (deterministic make_id) and the same fees_due (25.00 + 1,007.86 = 1,032.86). The terminal state is unique.
- **Load-bearing per edge** (skip one write and replay, auditor's recomputation): gold plan 355.25; skip mileage gives 194.83; skip wear gives 416.60; skip fee gives 403.93. Every edge bears weight.
- **Tools do not judge prerequisites.** The `pay_return_balance_installment_2f123e0a` body books the payment and fee-payment rows and lowers fees_due, with no read of return_charge rows and no status check. The charge tools likewise do not check status or dispute timing.
- **Persona.**
  - The persona raises only the root ("make today's payment on the turned-in car's final bill, nothing else").
  - "You know there is a final bill coming … nothing has shown up yet" is background only and is not in the scripted opening line.
  - The conditional line "If the agent tells you something has to be put on your account or worked out before today's payment can be set … go ahead" is passive and fires only on the agent's statement. It does not name a charge.
  - The persona closes after the payment confirmation, which is where the derived solution ends.
- The tree derived from policy and world alone matches the declared `prerequisite` field.
